categories.main_business_segments: The Scotts Miracle-Gro Company operates through three reportable segments: U.S. Consumer (consumer lawn and garden business in the United States), Hawthorne (indoor and hydroponic gardening business), and Other (primarily consumer lawn and garden business in Canada). Corporate includes general and administrative expenses not allocated to the segments.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company manufactures, markets, and sells branded lawn and garden products, including fertilizers, grass seed, growing media, controls (herbicides, pesticides, rodent control), hydroponic nutrients, and lighting systems. Production relies on proprietary formulations, patented dispensing devices, and advanced hydroponic and lighting technologies, with a focus on quality, innovation, and supply chain efficiency.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers are large home improvement retailers (notably The Home Depot and Lowe’s, which together accounted for 48% of 2024 net sales), mass merchandisers, warehouse clubs, hardware chains, garden centers, e-commerce platforms, and hydroponic product distributors. End markets include residential consumers, indoor growers, and commercial horticulture operations.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s primary operations are in North America, with the U.S. as the largest market. It also has a presence in Canada (via the Other segment), and operates manufacturing, distribution, and R&D facilities in the U.S., Canada, the Netherlands, Mexico, and China. International sales are a smaller portion of total revenue.
categories.supply_chain_position: Scotts Miracle-Gro operates primarily downstream in the supply chain, focusing on manufacturing, marketing, and distributing finished branded consumer products to retailers and distributors. It also acts as an exclusive agent for Monsanto’s consumer Roundup products, providing marketing and distribution services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include maintaining market leadership through brand strength, product innovation, and supply chain optimization. R&D focuses on new product development, improved formulations, packaging, and manufacturing processes, with annual R&D spending of $34.6 million in 2024. The company is also investing in digital marketing, sustainability, and expanding its proprietary hydroponic brands.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through the sale of branded consumer products to retailers and distributors. Additional revenue streams include commissions and reimbursements from the exclusive marketing agreement for Monsanto’s consumer Roundup products, as well as equity income from joint ventures like Bonnie Plants.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include Spectrum Brands, Central Garden & Pet, Kellogg Garden Products, Oldcastle Retail, Lebanon Seaboard, Reckitt Benckiser, FoxFarm, Nanolux, Sun Gro Horticulture, Advanced Nutrients, SBM Life Science, Woodstream, Sunday Lawn Care, and Hydrofarm. Scotts Miracle-Gro is the market leader in U.S. consumer lawn and garden, with strong brand recognition and broad distribution.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For fiscal 2024, net sales were $3.55 billion, flat year-over-year after a 9.5% decline in 2023. The company reported a net loss of $34.9 million in 2024, a significant improvement from a $380.1 million loss in 2023, driven by lower impairment and restructuring charges. The U.S. Consumer segment is the largest, while Hawthorne has faced sales declines due to cannabis market oversupply.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Scotts Miracle-Gro emphasizes trusted, widely recognized brands (Scotts, Miracle-Gro, Ortho, Tomcat, Roundup) and product performance, supported by innovation, quality, and strong retailer relationships. Differentiation is driven by proprietary technologies, comprehensive product lines, and a focus on consumer education, sustainability, and in-store support.
